column1: # tools/rlxfw-marks-absent.tsv -- the vendor kernels `rlxfw-marks.py verify`
# reads as `--absent`, declared by path, size and sha256.  RUNSHEET `P10`.
# `tools/rlxfw-kbuild.sh` reads this file twice.  Before it stages a tree it
# checks every row against the file on disk and refuses the build -- exit 3,
# naming the row -- if a file is missing or has another size or another
# sha256.  After the build it checks them again, at the point of use, and
# passes each one to `verify` as `--absent`.  A row that does not verify is
# never skipped: `verify` with nothing to be absent from can only say
# *present in mine*, which is a label and not a discriminator.
# The bytes never enter this repository.  One file is this unit's own kernel,
# decompressed from its flash dump; the other is someone else's property.
# Paths are relative to $FWRE_WORK.
# WHY UNDER tools/ AND NOT config/.  Every file under config/ is hashed into
# RECIPE_ID, which is compiled into every object as RLXFW_SRC_ID and printed
# by `ID0`: it names what an image is built FROM.  This list changes no byte
# of any image; it is what an image is compared AGAINST.  Under config/, an
# edit here would move ID0, recompile all 592 objects (`INC-1`) and change
# the image with its content unchanged, and every image's identity would
# depend on where on this desk a vendor file sits.  `tools/binsim-corpus.tsv`
# has the same shape -- vendor artefacts under $FWRE_WORK, declared by length
# and sha256 beside the tool that reads them -- and lives here for the same
# reason.
# Columns, tab separated; every field non-empty:
#   name   relpath (under $FWRE_WORK)   bytes   sha256   role
# WHERE EACH VALUE COMES FROM
#   unit-kernel  量 2026-09-23 from the file: 3,374,772 bytes and the digest
#                below.  Second source: `notes/cache-model.md`'s 2026-08-26
#                record of the same decompression (size and full sha256),
#                which `tools/hazlint` also pins as KERNEL_SHA / KERNEL_SIZE.
#   drop-kernel  量 2026-09-23 from the file: 2,953,660 bytes and the digest
#                below -- the first full sha256 of this file in the
#                repository; `notes/kernel-build.md` § 13 carries its first
#                16 hex digits, 48b1a17187bcc729, and they agree.  Second
#                source: the clone `src-vendor/CLONED.tsv` pins at 5c9be5d9
#                records this path as git blob ffe28e9017c2fc8a8e96a462fc367b2ee9d5bbca,
#                and `git hash-object` of the file on disk reproduces it.
# 🔴 Two rows with one digest are one artefact counted twice, and the driver
# refuses them.  `P6` carried exactly that for a day: two of its three "vendor
# artefacts" were one kernel, one of them compressed (2026-08-29, `R3-7`).
# WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT ESTABLISH
#   * That no other vendor kernel holds a mark string.  The first row is the
#     one the anti-DoD needs -- the kernel the loader re-stages at 0x80500000
#     is this unit's -- and the second is breadth, a genuinely different build.
#   * Anything about a compressed image.  A count over an LZMA stream is 0 for
#     every image, this project's own `nfjrom` included (`P10`, 2026-08-29), so
#     no compressed file may be listed here: it is a leg that cannot fail.
#   * That the uploaded image carries the marks.  `verify` reads the linked
#     ELF; `P10`'s flat-image leg is not automated by anything.
# name
unit-kernel
column5: this unit's own vendor kernel, decompressed from its flash dump (r0-vendor-kernel.bin)
